user_query: Why does the passage claim node2vec generalizes prior work, and what limitation of earlier feature learning approaches does it address?
llm_response: The passage says node2vec generalizes prior work because it can recover both breadth-first and depth-first neighborhood exploration as special cases of its biased random walks, rather than committing to only one fixed notion of a node’s neighborhood. It addresses the limitation of earlier feature learning approaches that used a single, rigid neighborhood definition or sampling strategy, which made them unable to adapt to different structural roles and community patterns in graphs.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a standard description of node2vec’s contribution and limitation addressed, and it matches the commonly cited formulation in the original paper.
